C000.label: How to Read a Recursive Book
C000.desc: chapter "How to Read a Recursive Book" (FRONT MATTER; paragraphs [P0001] to [P0023])

modeler: Aim (get you to your first page) is clear and the tonight test is checkable. But the doors, caution and sentence setup overlap; trim, and name a stock somewhere.
skeptic: Aim (get you to a first page) is clear and Maya helps, but the thesis sentence and caveat bolt on late; the closing test at least names its own failure.
clinician: Aim (get you to a first page) is clear and kind. But routes, sources caution and slogan pile up; the long reading list is pure reception. Cut P0009/P0017 duplication.
habit: Good: a door, a tonight test with a fail condition. But the circle point repeats across P0002-4 and the caution; trim to one pass.
contemplative: Its one job is clear, and the sentence test is small. But warning, orders, doors, caveat all stack. Keep the doors; fold the rest into fewer breaths.
stress: Aim is clear and the 'count against the book' test has teeth. But order, doors and one-sentence pitch overlap; the Maya return is nice, pitch less so. Trim.
gamedesigner: Aim is clear and the three doors give a choice. But Loop Tongue and Standing Thirds are front-loaded jargon, and the caution paragraph delays play.
structural: Aim is getting you to a first page; Maya planted at open and paid off at the close. Test tonight has a failure sign. Solid scaffold.
satirist: Aim is plain: get you to page one. But Maya, the second-reading promise and the 'scaffolding' line say the same thing three times. Merge them.
mythmaker: Maya in her sister quarrel is a face, and June pays off. But P0003 and P0017 run on abstractions with nobody in them.

modeler: One job is stated early and Maya's river returns. But the test appears four times (P0003, P0018, P0022, P0023) and P0019 is a tangent. Merge the tests into one.
skeptic: Aim is stated early. But Maya's June recurs, and the phone rep and design caveat drift. The test has a falsifier, yet 'we build the world' stays asserted, not argued.
clinician: Clear one job and a kind, losable test. But the arcs point is made twice, Maya's June twice, and Third Thing and Standing Thirds are used before taught.
habit: Good: one rep tonight, a sentence that can lose. But limits, caution and Part names pile up before the doors; trim to one cue and one door per breath.
contemplative: Aim is plain and Maya's margin test is doable. But the caution, the limit and the one-sentence slogan crowd the page, and P0003, P0022 and P0023 repeat each other. Trim to one door's worth.
stress: Page promises 'one job' but also carries warning, arcs, doors, caveat, book sentence and test. Break it into fewer jobs. Ending's falsifiable test and Maya's June land well.
gamedesigner: Aim is clear and the margin test is a real move. But the tutorial front-loads Loop Tongue, Standing Thirds and Weavings, and P0018 and P0019 are side warnings. Trim to the door choice.
structural: Job stated up front, and the test can lose. But Maya's June is told three times, and the limit paragraph and doors arrive out of order. Merge the Maya repeats; put the limit before the doors.
satirist: Aim is stated twice, which is once too often. 'Second reading works' recurs in P2, P5, P12. Loop Tongue, Standing Thirds, Weavings are used before taught. Prune and fold.
mythmaker: Maya's June frames it and returns at the end, earned. But the three doors and the caveats are abstract. Give each door a reader with something at stake.

modeler: Good stock: 'each pass leaves a deposit.' But the page's 'one job' gets crowded by cautions, limits and the one-sentence book. Trim to what reaches page one.
skeptic: Aim is stated and the ending returns to Maya with a test that can lose. But the arcs paragraphs and door descriptions overlap; tighten to one.
clinician: Safe on a bad day: 'hand got there first counts', 'never your fault', and a failable one-rep test. Returns to Maya in June. Minor: margin-rereading nudges self-scrutiny.
habit: Great: a rep for tonight, a cue (hand before phone), a result that counts. Cautions, doors and the sentence each read as separate jobs; fold them under the rep.
contemplative: The aim is plain and the rep can fail. But arcs, three doors, two cautions and the sentence say it all twice. Say each once, gently.
stress: Rare: it can lose. One job stated, a phone rep, a margin note, 'count that against the book.' Maya's June pays off. Calm-sea claim, but it admits the storm.
gamedesigner: Clear one-job opener and a rep to run now. But the two cautions are a side quest from getting-to-page-one; tighten or fold into the doors.
structural: One job stated up front, Maya returns in June, test can fail. Whose rules? P0019 names design but offers no lever a group could pull; add one.
satirist: One job, plainly stated, and a rep that can fail. But the thesis sentence, two cautions and three doors crowd a 'first page' page; P0004 and P0005 repeat the arcs point. Trim.
mythmaker: Maya planted at the start and returned to in June is a real arc. But the reading-order and caution paragraphs have nobody in them; give the cautions a face.

C002.label: 1. What You Already Know
C002.desc: chapter "1. What You Already Know" (PART ONE — WHY THIS MATTERS; paragraphs [P0028] to [P0034])

modeler: Lawn path is a real local-rule case with a footstep to catch. P0027, P0028 and P0029 restate one claim; also name what stops a path growing.
skeptic: Aim is clear and the footstep test can fail. But it tells readers what they have felt without support, and it closes on 'the rest of the book falls out', which is oversold.
clinician: The lawn path returns at the close, which is a good landing. But P0028 and P0029 restate P0027. 'Find your footstep' on Sunday dread hints the dread is your doing. Pick a neutral example.
habit: Test one solid thing, find the footstep, catch it once today; a failure condition is stated. Lawn opening returns at the close with weight. Fine.
contemplative: The lawn path opens and closes it, and the check is small and falsifiable. P0028 repeats P0027 and P0029 repeats P0028. Keep one, and say it once.
stress: Good: the bridge exception names a break condition, and the 'can't find a repeating act, the claim failed' test is real. But P0028 restates P0025 and P0027 at equal strength; merge them.
gamedesigner: Strong hook: the lawn path returns as a footstep test with a fail state. P0027 and P0028 state the same claim twice; merge them.
structural: One test, one aim, and the lawn footstep returns at the close. But P0028 restates P0027 at equal strength, and 'worn path' ignores who paved it.
satirist: The lawn path is a real image and the test can fail. But the fern is a tangent, 'built small' is said three times, and 'the rest of the book falls out' is Bokonon-grade overreach.
mythmaker: The lawn path and the footstep return nicely. But 'built small', 'weather' and the claim restate one point three times. Give the Sunday dread a face.

modeler: The lawn path is a real loop: wear makes steps likelier, and it stops when the shortcut stops paying. The footstep test can fail. Good napkin sketch; name the stock (worn ground) outright.
skeptic: One aim, and the footpath gives a causal account with a failure condition. But the fern is decoration, and the path paragraphs overlap. 'Never built in one stroke' is asserted, not checked.
clinician: Safe and small: find one footstep, no blame, and a stated way to fail. The fern is decoration and the lawn has no person in it; give it one.
habit: Clear aim and a doable footprint hunt with a fail condition. Phone, fern and five-years-ago stack three examples; give one person, Maya, the whole chapter.
contemplative: Clear aim, small footstep to catch today, and it can fail. The fern and the second path restatement in P0033 are decoration; let the path carry it alone.
stress: Aim is clear and the footstep test can fail. But the fern line is decoration, and the path claim leans on one lawn; give a person a footstep.
gamedesigner: Tight level: lawn path, find the footstep, can fail. P0030 stacks phone, fern and past self; keep one image. Ending returns to the path with weight.
structural: Lawn path is a clean mechanism with a failure condition. The fern leaflet is decoration, and the solid-thing claim is stated twice. Rework the fern into the path or drop its function.
satirist: Path-on-lawn is concrete and the test can fail. But the fern is decoration with no measurement, and P31 and P33 make the same claim with only 'you' standing in it.
mythmaker: The lawn path is a good image and it returns. But nobody walks it. Put a named person on the shortcut, with something to lose.

C003.label: 2. The Third Thing
C003.desc: chapter "2. The Third Thing" (PART ONE — WHY THIS MATTERS; paragraphs [P0035] to [P0053])

modeler: Coastline, die, thresholds, chairs, bees, essentialism: many aims, with tangents and a landing. Needs splitting. Third Thing still lacks a named stock or loop.
skeptic: Emergence, forces, essentialism, two senses of 'real': four aims. Analogy is asserted as ontology. Split the chapter; keep the die, which can actually be checked.
clinician: Emergence, symphysical, thresholds, essentialism and two senses of real, all in one chapter. Bee and force pairs are tangents. Split it; give the marriage a face.
habit: Emergence, symphysical, two senses of real, essentialism: concept pile-up, bee tangent. The end exercise is fine but unanchored. Cut to one idea, one Monday-morning test.
contemplative: Beautiful pieces, too many: coastline, die, chair, bee, essentialism. 'Real' stretched thin. One idea, one practice would breathe. The closing Try this works.
stress: Third Thing, emergence, threshold, force pairs, essentialism, two senses of real: a pile. Bee tangent. Admits 'argument by likeness' yet never breaks it. Split it.
gamedesigner: Overloaded: die game, emergence, threshold, chair, bee, two senses of real, essentialism. Three concepts at once; split it. Try-this is good.
structural: Emergence, symphysical, thresholds, forces, two senses of real, essentialism: a list of topics. Bee and chair pairs repeat. Split it; give one case a face.
satirist: Coastline and die earn their keep. Then emergence, symphysical, two kinds of 'real', essentialism pile on. Split it; one idea per chapter.
mythmaker: Coastline, marriage, chair, bees, essentialism: too many aims. The marriage is the only blood in it. The two-description test works; cut the rest.

modeler: The Maya/Dan loop (wariness shortens the fuse) is a stock-and-flow. But threshold, skaters, bee, two senses of real and essentialism are stacked; P0049 packs three ideas. Cut to one or two.
skeptic: Aim and Maya/Dan are planted early, and the Try this can fail. But thresholds, force pairs, bees, two senses of 'real' and essentialism pile up. Trim to one chain.
clinician: Maya and Dan and the 'what does it need' test are humane. But thresholds, skaters, bee and real-as-occurrence stack up; the fear paragraph spikes hard. Trim, then move the fear piece.
habit: Five-minute two-descriptions test can fail, good. But skaters, bee, two kinds of real and essentialism bury it. Cut to one engine, one couple, then the test.
contemplative: The Try this is good and can fail. The body is too much: thresholds, chair, forces, bee, two kinds of real, essentialism. Several ideas arrive at once. Split it, and keep Maya and Dan.
stress: Aim is stated, and the list-versus-single-thing test can fail. But coastline, chair, bee and essentialism stack up; several are analogies sold as support. Trim to one case.
gamedesigner: Good hook and a Try this that can fail. In between: symphysical, emergence, forces, bees, two senses of real, essentialism. Difficulty spikes and idle reading; split the chapter.
structural: The aim is stated, then the body adds thresholds, forces, essentialism and two senses of 'real'. New terms arrive in clumps. Split the chapter. The pen-and-five-minutes test is good.
satirist: Aim is stated, then the chapter wanders: chair, forces, bee, two senses of 'real', essentialism. Symphysical, emergence, Third Thing arrive in a heap. Split it. Die test and Maya/Dan are good.
mythmaker: Maya and Dan open it and close it well. In the middle the chair, the bee and the two senses of 'real' crowd out the couple. Cut to one case.

modeler: Dice triangle and Maya's fuse-shortening loop are real machinery. But chair, forces, skaters, bee and essentialism stack as analogies; no balancing side. Cut to one mechanism.
skeptic: Aim is planted with Maya and Dan and the closing test can fail. But the bee, skaters, essentialism and two senses of real sprawl, and new terms stack up. Prune and pace.
clinician: Maya and Dan carry it, and the fear-is-real-but-not-proof passage is kind. But chair, forces, skaters, bee, essentialism and two senses of 'real' pile up; trim to one stack, one step.
habit: Maya/Dan and the pen test are usable. But bee, skaters, essentialism and two 'reals' pile concepts on; the middle drifts. Cut to one cue-linked path.
contemplative: The pen test is simple and can fail. But the chapter carries too much: emergence, symphysical, bees, two kinds of real, essentialism. Keep the chair, shed the rest.
stress: Die-and-pen test is checkable and Try-this can fail. But essentialism, two senses of 'real', and a speculative bee tangent sprawl past the aim. Cut or relocate them.
gamedesigner: Great die-and-pen playable test, and Try-this has a fail signal. Then symphysical, emergence, threshold, two reals, essentialism pile up; bee and skaters are side quests. Split.
structural: Aim stated, Maya and Dan carry it, but coastline, die game, chair, force pairs, bumblebee, two senses of real, essentialism pile up. Cut to one proof.
satirist: Die-and-pen triangle is real Bryson; Maya and Dan carry it. But symphysical, emergence, essentialism, two kinds of real arrive stacked, and bee speculation is padding. Busy, busy, busy.
mythmaker: Maya and Dan are a good spine, then vanish for the chair, skaters, bee and essentialism. Cut the tangents back to them; one concept at a time.

C005.label: 4. The Three Pillars
C005.desc: chapter "4. The Three Pillars" (PART ONE — WHY THIS MATTERS; paragraphs [P0064] to [P0077])

modeler: Too many concepts at once: pillars, Nest, leverage, perspective, Standpoint, chance, worth. Charging-phone test with a one-week check is good. Split it; each pillar needs its stock and delay.
skeptic: The phone-in-another-room test is checkable. Yet pillars, Standpoint, chance and worth arrive in a rush, and the lawn, Nest and lateness paragraphs repeat one move.
clinician: Phone-in-another-room step is small, with a falsifier and 'worth is yours'. But Standpoint, leverage, chance, worth crowd in; P0064/65/70 overlap. Give each a person.
habit: No single aim; pillars, Nest, Standpoint and chance/worth pile up. Phone-charging test is a real rep with a fail rule. Name one aim and trim.
contemplative: Too much for one exhale: pillars, Nest, Standpoint, chance, worth, new names. The charger test is lovely. Let the chapter hold fewer things.
stress: Three pillars, Standpoint, chance and worth: too many aims. The phone-in-another-room test can fail, but the 'worth is yours' close is comfort. Split or narrow.
gamedesigner: Difficulty spike: Third Thing, Global Form, Local Rule, Nest, Leverage, Perspective, Standpoint, chance and worth stack up. Split it. The phone-charging test works.
structural: Reads as a list: three pillars, Standpoint, leverage, perspective, chance, worth. P0065 and P0070 repeat points. Phone test is good but bolted on. Trim and stage the concepts.
satirist: Phone-charging test is good. But Pillars, Standpoint, Leverage, Perspective, Core Line, chance, worth, Dyad, Skein, all in one chapter. Busy, busy, busy. Teach fewer.
mythmaker: The lawn path is a good image, but Standpoint, Leverage, Perspective, chance and worth pile in together. Too many abstractions, nobody standing in them; one person, fewer ideas.

modeler: Dana's phone gives a testable loop and a leverage claim. But the pillars, Nest, Dyad/Skein names, Standpoint, chance and worth arrive in a rush, and P0069-70 repeat. Pace it.
skeptic: Dana's phone test is checkable, with a causal cue story and a stated failure. But three pillars, Standpoint, chance and worth arrive at once. Split or cut.
clinician: Dana's phone-in-the-hall step is small, falsifiable and blame-free. But Global Form, Dyad, Skein, Standpoint and Core Line arrive in clumps; chance and worth feel bolted on.
habit: Dana's phone-in-hall test, tally and failure rule are exactly right. Ahead of it, Standpoint, Core Line, chance and worth arrive at once; teach fewer, later.
contemplative: Dana and the phone test are warm and doable. But Nest, Dyad, Skein, leverage, perspective, chance and worth arrive crowded, and the pillars are retold twice. Fewer words, one idea per breath.
stress: Dana stands in it and the phone-in-hall test can fail within a week. The Nest paragraph piles rung names and a caveat at once; teach them separately.
gamedesigner: Dana plus the phone test gives a playable save point. But three pillars, Standpoint, leverage, perspective, chance and worth arrive in one run. Too many rules at once; stage them.
structural: Dana anchors it and the phone test can fail. But Global Form, Local Rule, Dyad, Skein and Culture arrive at once in one paragraph, and chance and worth are tacked on. Teach the terms singly.
satirist: Dana carries it, and the nightstand test can fail. But Global Form, Local Rule, Dyad, Skein, Standpoint, Core Line pile up in one page. Busy, busy, busy. Teach fewer.
mythmaker: Dana stands in every pillar, and her hand on the empty nightstand pays off the opening. Dense, but a face carries it. Nearly there.

modeler: Phone-away test with a tally and a 'push too near a leaf' fallback is a real experiment. But Nest hands over Global Form, Local Rule and three rung names at once; chance/worth is orphaned.
skeptic: Dana's test is small, causal and can fail, and the honest 'a guess until tested' helps. But Nest, Global Form, Local Rule and three rung names arrive at once; the reach/view/chance paragraphs repeat.
clinician: Dana stands in every pillar and ends on her empty nightstand. 'Nobody's fault' and a failable phone test are safe. Reach-outruns-view warning could shame; keep the kindness line.
habit: Dana's phone-in-the-hall is exactly the rep I want: cue, tally, failure signal. Standpoint, chance, worth arrive late and crowded; trim before the test.
contemplative: The phone in the hall is a small, honest practice, with a way to fail. But pillars, Standpoint, chance and worth arrive crowded. Offer one pillar per breath.
stress: Dana stands in it and the phone-in-hall test can fail, with a week's tally. But Nest paragraph stacks Global Form, Local Rule, Dyad, Skein, Culture at once.
gamedesigner: Dana's phone test is a real move with a fail signal. But the Nest paragraph drops five terms at once, a difficulty spike; chance/worth paragraph is a rulebook aside.
structural: Dana anchors a clear one-page aim; phone-in-hall test is checkable. Still, a charging spot is a private lever; name the platform's design as owner.
satirist: Dana's phone gives it a face and the test can fail. Yet Global Form, Local Rule, Nest, Standpoint, Core Line arrive as capitalized authorities; P0069-70 and P0076 restate. Trim.
mythmaker: Dana stands in every pillar and the empty nightstand pays off. But the Nest paragraph piles Local Rule, Global Form and three rung names at once; unpack it.

C009.label: 8. Complicated or Complex
C009.desc: chapter "8. Complicated or Complex" (PART ONE — WHY THIS MATTERS; paragraphs [P0108] to [P0131])

modeler: Feedback question is a real test, and the reset is the balancing side. Go, tax-code and 80/20 digressions dilute it. Show one pond's stock and delay.
skeptic: The feedback question and Friday-record test are falsifiable. Go, rule-multiplication, chaos and 80/20 are separate chapters' worth; the pond claim needs a second payload cut or reworked.
clinician: Friday-argument test is concrete and kind. But Go, elegance, chaos and 80/20 sprawl past car-versus-pond; three Go paragraphs. Split the chapter or cut to one case.
habit: Friday-argument test with a scheduled reset is good. Go, tax code, 80/20 and arithmetic pile up; each needs a person and a job.
contemplative: The feedback question is clear and usable. Go, tax code, multiplication and 80/20 wander. Keep one example, trim the rest.
stress: Feedback question is testable (fix came back = pond). But Go, tax code, 80/20 and emergence limits sprawl; 80/20 claim is one anecdote-grade mechanism. Tighten.
gamedesigner: Clear feedback test, but Go, the tax code, 80/20 and the reset detour pile up. Concepts arrive too fast and the Try this comes late.
structural: Promises one question, then wanders through complication, elegance, Go, pair arithmetic, chaos and 80/20. Three Go paragraphs are a tangent. Pond test is usable. Cut to the feedback question.
satirist: Promises one question, then wanders through Go, 80/20, chaos and elegance. Go earns a Bryson fact, twice over. Split the chapter. Friday reset test is usable.
mythmaker: Car and pond is lovely, but Go, arithmetic, chaos and 80/20 wander off with no one living in them. Cut to one person with a returning Friday argument.

modeler: The feedback question is a clean structural test, and the Try-this reset can fail. But Go, elegance, 80/20 and chaos form a long detour. Reinforcing loop is named; balancing limit is not.
skeptic: Aim is the feedback question, then drifts into Go, elegance, chaos and 80/20. Try this is falsifiable, but the body stretches the claim past its aim; cut or relocate.
clinician: Priya's Friday and the calendar reset are usable, with a failure branch. Go, tax code, 80/20 and chaos sprawl past one question; cut to what serves it.
habit: Friday-argument reset on the calendar is a real rep, and Priya closes well. Go, 80/20, chaos and elegance sprawl between; keep one feedback question.
contemplative: The feedback question is clear and Priya's Friday is a fine practice. But elegance, Go, pair-counting, chaos, 80/20 and resets each pull away from it. Return to one question.
stress: Priya's return-of-fix test is checkable and the ending pays off. Go, rule-pair arithmetic, chaos and concentration drift from the feedback question; one is enough.
gamedesigner: Priya's return is a strong hook and the closing test pays off. The Go detour, arithmetic, chaos and 80/20 spike difficulty and sprawl. Cut to one engine.
structural: Feedback test is the aim, but four Go paragraphs, elegance, 80/20 and chaos pull away from it. The rotating-meeting reset is a real lever. Cut or move the Go run.
satirist: Aim is the feedback question, but then Go, elegance, tax code, 80/20 and chaos pile in. Priya's Friday ending is earned, yet the middle shuffles freely. Trim to one example.
mythmaker: Priya's Friday argument opens and closes it. In between, Go, tax codes and chaos wander off with no one in them. Bring Priya back through the middle.

modeler: Feedback question plus Priya's recurring Friday is a testable reading of the loop, and the reset is a balancing flow. But elegance, Go, rule-pairs, chaos and 80/20 sprawl; pare back.
skeptic: The feedback question is checkable against the record, and the reset test can fail. The chess, pair-count, chaos and 80/20 asides pile concepts after the aim; trim or move them.
clinician: Priya's Friday is a good anchor and the reset step is small and testable. But Go, rule arithmetic, chaos, 80/20 sit as separate detours; the middle idles. Cut to one.
habit: One question, one scheduled reset: good. Go, chaos, 80/20 and the tax code detour from it. Keep one example, then land on Priya's Friday.
contemplative: The feedback question is clear and Friday's reset is doable. But Go, arithmetic, chaos and 80/20 pull away from the aim. Return to Priya and trim.
stress: Priya's Friday record is a real test that can fail. But Go, tax code, 80/20 and the reset exit sprawl past 'does it feed back?' Trim to that.
gamedesigner: Feedback question is a clean tool and Priya's Friday returns well. The middle is a long cutscene: Go, chess, rule arithmetic, chaos, 80/20. Cut to one worked case.
structural: Feedback question is clear and Priya's Friday returns. But Go, rule arithmetic, 80/20, chaos and reset schedule are five side-trips; trim to two.
satirist: Car versus pond is a bar-proof question, and Go is delightful. But elegance arithmetic, 80/20, chaos and the exit paragraph wander from the feedback question. Cut to one.
mythmaker: Priya's returning Friday argument closes the loop well. But Go, the rule arithmetic and the 80/20 stretch have no one standing in them; give Go a player.

C010.label: 9. Position, Speed, Acceleration
C010.desc: chapter "9. Position, Speed, Acceleration" (PART ONE — WHY THIS MATTERS; paragraphs [P0132] to [P0161])

modeler: Closest to machinery: lag, doubling time, natural period, a stop-here rule, a falsifiable date. Still lacks a limit on growth; add the balancing cap.
skeptic: Read, push, wait and commitment-pairs are four aims. The cabin return earns something, but the Try this mid-chapter splits the build; rule of 70 gives a real date.
clinician: Dated three-line page and rule-of-70 falsifier are usable. But the commitments stretch is a second chapter, and Try this lands mid-chapter. Move it out; keep the seat ending.
habit: Three-line page, dated and re-read after one period, is usable. Rule of 70, calendar and recursion paragraphs crowd it; cut to what the page needs.
contemplative: The three-line page is a real act, with a seat image to close. Rule of 70, clocks and recursion crowd the path to it.
stress: Three-line log with a dated recheck is testable, and the rule-of-70 'change the force' trigger breaks cleanly. But period, doubling, lag and derivatives pile up; the cabin ending feels borrowed.
gamedesigner: Good three-line tracker with a date check, and the cabin return pays off. But period, doubling time, rule of 70 and the calendar overlap; trim.
structural: Cabin return lands well and the three-line test is usable. The commitments-pairs run and the P0150/P0151 double stop-here are padding mid-chapter. Relocate or merge.
satirist: Reading, pushing, lag and commitment-pairs are several chapters in a trench coat. The seat-pressing cabin close is earned. Three-line dated page is a real test.
mythmaker: The plane seat and the closing cabin are a lovely rhyme. But the middle sprawls (calendar yeses, rule of 70) with no face; pick one person's savings.

modeler: Good stock/flow/lag bones and a dated, falsifiable page. But commitments-pairs detour and twin 'stop at acceleration' paragraphs repeat; the middle shuffles. Merge them, tie pairs to the stock.
skeptic: Dated three-line page is testable and admits 'you misread'. But P0158/P0159 repeat, the commitments detour and two Try-thises pad it; rework to one throughline.
clinician: Dana and cabin frame it well, and the dated three-line page is safe on a bad day. But rule of 70, pair-cost arithmetic and rates-of-rates sprawl; trim or move.
habit: Strong: three-line page, Dana's flat Fridays, five-minute tonight rep. But the commitments-in-pairs stretch is a detour from the page; fold it into the lag or lift it.
contemplative: Aim is clear and the dated three-line page is doable. But commitments, rule of 70 and recursion pile on; the breath breaks. Trim to the page.
stress: Aim is stated and Dana's flat Fridays plus the rule-of-70 exit ('change the force') can fail. But the commitments detour and the twin 'stop at acceleration' paragraphs pad; the order sprawls.
gamedesigner: Great hook: three-line page, Dana's dated rereads give real feedback. But pairs-of-commitments and recursion stretches are side quests, and 'third line' is waiting in one place, acceleration in another.
structural: Three-line page aim is clear and testable. But yes-pairs, rule of 70 and recursion detours pile on after the Try-this; landing arrives twice. Fold or cut them.
satirist: Aim is stated plainly and Dana's Fridays help. But commitments-in-pairs, rule of 70 and the clock pile on; ladder and doubling paragraphs repeat. Cut the calendar detour.
mythmaker: Dana and the cabin seat give it blood, and the three-line page is a real payload. But the rules-pairs detour, the doubled stop-at-acceleration paragraphs and the orphan calendar line sprawl.

modeler: Position/speed/acceleration is a real stock-flow ladder, good. But doubling time, nested rates, Dana, and belief-free asides pile up; the delay arrives late. Order is shufflable; tighten.
skeptic: Dated page with a falsifiable reread is good. But period, doubling time, pair-costs and rates-of-rates crowd in; the commitments run is a tangent, and two concepts arrive per paragraph.
clinician: Aim and Dana's flat Fridays are safe and concrete; the yes-lag detour and the recursion pair pad it, and the period and doubling ideas arrive crowded. Trim, then reorder.
habit: Aim is stated and Try-this is a five-minute, dated, falsifiable rep. But the commitment-pairs detour and rates-of-rates sprawl, and period plus doubling time land together. Cut or trim.
contemplative: Aim and Dana's page are clear and the dated reread works. But period, doubling time, commitment pairs and rates-of-rates crowd in; cut to one thread.
stress: Aim is stated, but commitments-pairs, rule of 70 and rates-of-rates sprawl away from it. Close with a dated reread and a flat-date falsifier is solid; trim the detours.
gamedesigner: Aim and Dana's dated page are clear, and the try-this has a check date. But period, doubling time and pair-cost stack up as a difficulty spike. Trim the pairs tangent.
structural: Aim is clear and the page is testable. But the commitment-pairs and rates-of-rates stretches wander, and period plus doubling time arrive together. Cut or move them. Private page only, no lever.
satirist: The dated page is concrete and checkable, and Dana's flat Fridays help. But rule of 70, Nest recursion and the commitments pile all crowd in; P0158 and P0159 say the same thing. Trim to one thread.
mythmaker: Dana and the cabin seat give it faces and a return. But the commitments-pairs and rates-of-rates stretches feel like borrowed tangents; give them Dana's stakes or fold them in.

C012.label: 11. A Word on Belief Itself
C012.desc: chapter "11. A Word on Belief Itself" (PART ONE — WHY THIS MATTERS; paragraphs [P0173] to [P0192])

modeler: Opens with checking beliefs, then sprawls: not-self-help, not-care, what belief is for, disagreement shapes. Split it. The where-did-you-get-it test is small and falsifiable.

clinician: Aim splits into checking, what the book is not, what belief is for, and collisions. The care passage is vital but interrupts, and 'you have passed on a story' blames. The where-did-you-get-it step is good.
habit: One job is promised, then care limits, belief's purpose, collisions and a company example pile on. Split or cut to the check. The 'where did you get it' step is usable.
contemplative: Opens as 'how to hold a belief', then turns to self-help, care, two halves, disagreement. Too many rooms. Keep one thread; the care caution repeats itself.
stress: Aim is stated, then chapter sprawls: Snow Crash, not-self-help, not-care, belief's purpose, disagreement. P0175 'believe something' contradicts the checking aim. Split or trim. Origin-check test is breakable.

satirist: Bokonon nod earns a smile, but then it's a pile: not self-help, not care, farmers, 'family' companies. Aim is promised and drifts. Pick one. Busy, busy, busy.
mythmaker: Promises one job, then wanders: not self-help, not care, what belief is for, collisions. Snow Crash and the two farmers lack faces. Pick one aim; let the first-job example recur.

modeler: Aim is stated but the chapter wanders: origin, memes, care limits, two halves, collisions. Belief is never a stock with a loop. Cut to one thread; Dana's source test is usable.
skeptic: The Dana source test is checkable, with pass and fail stated. But care limits, purpose and disagreement shapes pull the aim apart, and 'two paragraphs on' is a forward pointer.
clinician: Care-limit paragraphs are exactly right, and Dana's two-minute source test is safe. But the aim splits across belief-origin, treatment limits, two halves and collisions; split the chapter.
habit: The source-and-who-serves check is a real two-minute rep with a fail sign. Then dementia, crisis, collision shapes pile on; aim splits. Split or trim.
contemplative: Dana's two-minute source check is good practice. But care, treatment, purpose of belief and collisions crowd one job; 'two paragraphs on' flags the strain. Split.
stress: Dana's source test can fail ('everyone knows'). But the chapter promises one job and delivers four: care limits, purpose of belief, collisions. Cut or relocate those.
gamedesigner: Strong test: source plus saw/told, with a clear failure signal. Lands back on Dana. But Snow Crash, collisions and the for-whom detour are extra levels nobody asked me to play.
structural: Check-your-source aim is stated, and the two-minute saw/told test can fail. But the care disclaimer, self-help contrast and collision shapes interrupt the build. Cluster the detours.
satirist: Opens with one job, then wanders into care-not-treatment, what belief is for, and farmers' wells. Dana's source test is usable. Split off the disclaimer and the collisions.
mythmaker: Dana's one-hour rule is the face; the ending returns to her. Lovely. But the care disclaimer, the not-self-help paragraph and the repeated test-by-practice paragraphs are padding. Trim them.

modeler: Aim is stated, then drifts: provenance, Snow Crash spread, mental-health caveat, two-halves, collisions. No stock or loop for belief; Dana's source test is usable but metaphor-heavy.
skeptic: Belief-checking, what the book is, not-therapy, what belief is for, and disagreement are separate topics. The two-minute source test has a failure criterion; the ending doesn't return to Dana.
clinician: Dana's two-minute source test is a gentle, checkable step, and the stop-and-tell-a-person line is right. But origin, audience, treatment limits, disagreement and collisions sprawl; pick one aim.
habit: Dana's source-and-'saw/told' two-minute test is my kind of rep, with a pass/fail. But Snow Crash, Sabbath, wells and disclaimers pile on. Pick one thread.
contemplative: Two-minute source-and-saw/told test is practicable. But Snow Crash, safety disclaimers, farmers and Sabbaths drift; the chapter sprawls past its one job.
stress: Check-your-belief aim is clear and Dana's source test can fail. But Snow Crash, crisis caveat, dementia, Sabbath and shared-well pile on; ending's confidence outruns the body.
gamedesigner: Two-question check plus Dana's source/saw-or-told test is playable with a pass/fail signal. Snow Crash, disclaimers and the well-versus-standoff shapes feel like side quests.
structural: Check-your-source aim holds and Dana carries it. Snow Crash, the well/standoff shapes and mental-health caveats pile up. No whose-rules lever; 'for whom' stays personal. Trim.
satirist: Bokonon is the right patron and the 'saw or told' test works at a bar. Three safety paragraphs pile up mid-chapter and break the build. Compress to one.
mythmaker: Dana's one-hour rule is a fine face and the ending pays her off. But the aim sprawls into Snow Crash, crisis warnings, whose-benefit, and farmers; the aim must govern them.

mythmaker: Day 1's three catches is a clear small act. But the moves are explained twice, and Self/Dyad/Skein plus four moves land together. Merge the duplicates, defer the scales.

contemplative: Two aims: skim eleven shapes, and test one rule. The inversion is said twice (P0901, P0904). The Priya test is good and small; trim the repeat.

gamedesigner: Clear aim, Dara stands in every caution. But the cautions are parallel levels and could be shuffled; reception-heavy. Order them as a ramp. Say-your-expectation-first plus wince is a real feedback signal.
structural: Aim stated up front; each caution has a check; ends on Dara's wince as the sign. Mirror and confirmation paragraphs overlap slightly; no structural lever named.
satirist: Dara's nod is a good plain opening, and 'say it aloud first' passes the bar test. But the cautions are a shufflable list; the wince ending is earned yet the order isn't.
mythmaker: Dara's cheap nod opens and her wince closes it; lovely. But the tax problem and dripping tap have nobody in them. Give the complicated-problem warning a face.

C080.label: 0. What a Turning Is
C080.desc: chapter "0. What a Turning Is" (PART SEVEN — THE TURNINGS; paragraphs [P1044] to [P1058])

structural: One definition, one test, clear. But P1008 re-warns what P1005 said, and P1006 drops four moves at once. Seder-child Try-this is small and checkable.

mythmaker: The seder child is a strong image, and the Aimed question is a real test. But the four moves arrive at once and nobody stands in P1006-1007.

modeler: Four moves (Look, Plant, Tend, Thin) land in one paragraph before the tables teach them. Introduce one move per row. The seder child return is earned.

clinician: Seder child returns well and the minute-long exercise is gentle. But Global Form, three tests and four moves crowd the middle; teach the moves where used.

contemplative: The seder child returns warmly. But P1055 hands me four moves at once inside a definition, and 1046/1048 repeat the commemoration point. Slow down.
stress: Definition and test are clear and the seder child returns. But P1055 drops four moves at once, and commemoration, optional-menu and rot paragraphs repeat each other. Prune.
gamedesigner: Seder child bookends well and the Aimed test is usable. But P1055 dumps Look/Plant/Tend/Thin at once: a difficulty spike. Defer the four moves to the tables.
structural: Definition-plus-test aim holds and the seder child returns. But P1048 repeats P1047, P1052 and P1056 drift, and P1055 drops four moves at once. Trim and defer.
satirist: Seder child pays off at the end, nicely. Yet P1055 dumps Move, Look, Plant, Tend, Thin at once, and P1046/P1048/P1057 repeat each other. Trim and pace.

modeler: Definition plus three tests is usable, and the seder child returns. But the ending is paid by assertion, and 'Tend' loop and the move taxonomy arrive stacked. Little stock or limit.
skeptic: One definition, one test, and Try-this is observable with a stated failure sign. But 'togetherness multiplies' is asserted, and Look/Plant/Tend/Thin arrive in a single paragraph.

habit: Definition plus three tests is clear, and the Aimed question works as a rep. But P1055 drops four moves at once; defer them to the tables.
contemplative: One definition, one test, and the seder child returns. But it is crowded: Look, Plant, Tend, Thin arrive together, and the menu and shared-alone asides spread it thin. Slow down.
stress: Clear definition and a testable Try-this. But P1055 drops four moves (Look, Plant, Tend, Thin) at once, a learnability spike. Defer them to the tables.
gamedesigner: Strong aim and a playable Try-this test. But P1055 drops four moves, Global Form and Third at once, and P1056 is menu admin. Defer moves; fold the filler.

satirist: The child at the seder is a lovely return. But the four moves (Look, Plant, Tend, Thin) arrive in one paragraph, admitted as not needed yet. Busy, busy, busy. Cut or defer them.

C082.desc: chapter "2. The Twelve Private Turnings — Self" (PART SEVEN — THE TURNINGS; paragraphs [P1064] to [P1068])

modeler: Dana plants, fixes one thing, then returns with a countable check: shorter list or door shuts. Small stock, visible correction. Good bathtub. Table rows each add a distinct move.

clinician: Dana fixes one cabinet, leaves eight, and the number-based check treats failure as information. Small, humane, causal enough. Pick-tonight ending is earned.
habit: Dana's twenty-minute cabinet fix is a real rep. Number check, failure named, 'put a date on it' is the cue. Small and runnable.
contemplative: Plain and small: pick one row, Dana shows it, a number checks it. Dana picks a row before the reader sees the table; place her after it.
stress: Dana's countable list and 'door still shuts' can fail. But the chapter ends on a nudge to set a date, not a changed understanding. Only one row is worked.
gamedesigner: Dana gives a person, a twenty-minute fix, a number check and a failure reading. Pick-a-row-tonight is playable. Table is a menu, but the chapter closes on a dated action.
structural: Dana's Patch Audit gives a number and a failure signal. But she appears before the table that names her row, and the ending is an instruction, not arrival.
satirist: Dana's cabinet door is the best kind of fact: twenty minutes, one number. But twelve unexplained Thirds sit in a table, and the order could be shuffled. Define one row fully.

modeler: Dana's list shrinking is a countable stock with a drain; Marcus gives rest a loop. Table does the rest. A guilt-delay estimate would sharpen it.
skeptic: Dana's countable check is good. Marcus's guilt is unfalsifiable and left dangling, and 'predict the third' points at a table not yet read. Resolve Marcus.
clinician: Dana's countable check and permission to fail are good. Marcus's 'predict the third' is an unpaid quiz with no check of his own. Give him a step.
habit: Dana gives a countable check, Marcus a second face, and 'pick your row tonight, put a date on it' is a clean rep. Marcus has no check of his own.
contemplative: Small, doable: Dana fixes one cabinet door. A count shows whether it worked. Marcus's guilt at three o'clock is honest. Table is long but plain.
stress: Dana's list and count can fail, which I like. Marcus's guilt-at-three reading confirms itself whichever way it goes. Name what a miss looks like.
gamedesigner: Dana's count and Marcus's predict-the-third give agency; each row is a tryable level. Check is a number that can fail. Landing is modest but paid for.
structural: Clear aim; Dana and Marcus stand in it and the check is a count. Marcus's 'predict the third' is never paid off, so the ending is just 'pick yours'.
satirist: Dana's nine stopgaps, Marcus's unearned Sunday, a countable result and a stated way to fail. Bar-stool-survivable. The twelve-row table is a menu, not a mystery.
mythmaker: Dana and Marcus put faces on the table, and the count is a clear test. The Marcus prediction prompt is slightly abrupt, but it works.

C083.label: 3. The Dyad Turnings
C083.desc: chapter "3. The Dyad Turnings" (PART SEVEN — THE TURNINGS; paragraphs [P1069] to [P1073])

modeler: Dana and Mo give the loop a face: fight, cold evening, off-ramp, then a test at the next fight. Failure condition and help escape are named. Solid.
skeptic: Dana and Mo give a falsifiable outcome and a stop-and-get-help clause. 'The cooking is the off-ramp' is asserted, not shown, though the test would expose it.

contemplative: Dana and Mo make the pattern liveable, and the test is the next fight. The safety line arrives late and quietly; give it a little more weight.
stress: Dana and Mo carry the cause, the off-ramp and a falsifiable test, with 'try another row' and a stop-and-get-help line. Honest about failing. The 'warmer quiet' measure is soft.
gamedesigner: Dana and Mo example, a next-fight test, a failure branch and a safety exit. Nineteen-row table is a wall, but the worked case keeps it playable.
structural: Dana and Mo thread cue, table and test; the return to them lands. Next fight is a falsifiable check, with a safety exit for fear. Sound.
satirist: Dana and Mo get a testable off-ramp, and the safety line is wise. But eighteen rows could be shuffled and their Thirds are jargon. Name one worked row, not all eighteen.
mythmaker: Dana and Mo's cold evening is paid off by a warmer one or the same silence. The fear caveat is right; the cooking off-ramp lands.

modeler: Escalation off-ramp is a real balancing loop; Dana and Mo test is falsifiable. Ines and Theo adds a second row. Safety exit is right.
skeptic: Pattern-first selection is clear. Dana and Mo give a causal reason and a failure sign, plus a fear exit. Ines and Theo are never revisited; close them too.
clinician: Pattern-first cue, two named pairs, a falsifiable next-fight test, and a fear exit ('bring in help') make it safe. Warm and usable on a bad evening.
habit: The cue is the pattern, two pairs show it, and Dana and Mo get a falsifiable outcome. Ines and Theo lack a check; the fear caveat is right.
contemplative: Two couples, each cooking one dish; a cue you can feel, and a way to see it failed. The fear exception is kind. Table is long, not heavy.
stress: Pattern-as-cue aim, two named pairs, falsifiable test (fight ends sooner or not), and a fear exit. Sturdy; it admits misreads and sends them to another row.
gamedesigner: Two worked pairs, name-your-Third prompt, then table. Dana and Mo return with a pass/fail signal and a safety exit. Plays well.
structural: Cue-is-pattern aim, two pairs, table as shelf, and a return to Dana and Mo with a pass/fail test and a safety exit. Order builds.
satirist: Two pairs, two rows, a named test, and a fear exit. Cooking as off-ramp is practical and believable. Eighteen-row table is a catalogue, but the chapter earns it.
mythmaker: Dana and Mo, then Ines and Theo, make two pairs standing in two rows. The ending returns to the cold dinner with a test and a safety exit.

C085.label: 5. The Seven Great Days — Culture
C085.desc: chapter "5. The Seven Great Days — Culture" (PART SEVEN — THE TURNINGS; paragraphs [P1079] to [P1082])

modeler: Village at the fire asks one question, and the closing note returns to 'nobody at the fire can say when it fell'. A date, a year-on check and a wrong-anchor sign. Earned.
skeptic: The fire question and the 'write the date, check in a year' test are usable and falsifiable. Seven unrelated Thirds in a table never build, and the end is a caveat, not an arrival.
clinician: Write the date today, check in a year: small and testable. The village question is never answered, and the chapter ends on a note, not an arrival.
habit: The fire question and 'write down the date of that turn' are doable today. It ends on a note and a table, so no landing. Return to the fire.
contemplative: The village at the winter fire gives it a face, and the closing test (can anyone say when it fell?) can fail. One doubt: 'late spring' is not fixed to the sky.
stress: Village question helps, and 'nobody can say when it fell, move it' is a real failure sign. But 'Chapter 7 explains' is an unpaid forward reference, and it ends on a footnote.
gamedesigner: Village-at-the-fire image opens, and the closing note returns with a date to write down and a one-year wrongness check. Concrete small action, with failure signal.
structural: The village-at-the-fire question returns in the closing test, 'nobody at the fire can say when it fell'. Pick a row, date it, and move the anchor if it fails.
satirist: The village-at-the-fire question and the 'if nobody can say when it fell, move it' check are honest. But the seven-row table is shuffleable and the real payload hides in an italic coda.
mythmaker: The village at the winter fire is the image I wanted, and it returns at the close with a year-later test. Still no single named villager.

modeler: Amara's yearly fire question works as a slow-loop sampling cadence. Date, check and wrong-anchor failure sign are all there. Cost-of-growth row is nicely structural.
skeptic: Amara carries the whole chapter, and the winter-fire question returns at the end with a way to be wrong. The anchor note is overloaded, but it is usable.
clinician: Amara carries the idea; two-minute dating step with a year-on check. Slow feedback, but safe and small. 'Predict the third' is ambiguous; name the row.
habit: Amara's garden threads through, and the two-minute date-writing rep has a year-on test. P1082 is one long italic block; split it into steps.
contemplative: Amara's fire question is simple and warm. The closing anchor paragraph holds too many things at once; trim it to rain, date, question.
stress: Amara's garden carries it. The two-minute date step is small, and the year-on test is honest that a wrong anchor gets moved. Delayed feedback is the weak spot.
gamedesigner: Amara carries the chapter, predict-the-third is real agency, and the year-on fire question can show failure. Anchor paragraph is dense but earns its place.
structural: One yearly turn per slow pattern; Amara runs from the opening question through the table to her one date and one fire question. Tight, testable.
satirist: Amara's question is good, but a forty-plot garden is no Culture. The last italic block crams anchor advice, homework and a grand 'whole year' sign-off. Split it, land smaller.
mythmaker: Amara at the winter fire carries the chapter from question to table to one date and one question a year on. The italic anchor note runs long.

C089.label: 9. What Outlives the Ceremony
C089.desc: chapter "9. What Outlives the Ceremony" (PART SEVEN — THE TURNINGS; paragraphs [P1100] to [P1107])

modeler: Carrier idea is causal: the recipe survives only via someone at her elbow. P1046 and P1047 both run the recipe analogy; merge. Two-guest test is checkable. Ending lands well.

clinician: Two-guest test is small and falsifiable, and the closing is sober, not bypassing. P1046 and P1047 both tell the recipe-outlives-its-maker story; reduce to one.
habit: The two-guest Try this is a real test. The recipe ending pays off. But the recipe point appears twice in the opening paragraphs. Merge them.
contemplative: The elbow ending is earned, and the two-guests test is simple. The recipe, the Spark Feast and the comfort paragraphs circle one point three times. Trim to one.
stress: Two-guest test and the recipe needing someone at the elbow keep the comfort modest. But the Spark Feast legacy and the first-try paragraphs repeat the carrier point. Trim one.
gamedesigner: Two-guest test gives a matching signal for whether the aim travels. The recipe image carries it, but P1047 is long reception and the landing is a comfort, not proof.
structural: The ending is modest and earned, and the two-guest test can fail. But the recipe image runs through P1046, P1047 and P1049 at similar strength. Trim P1047.
satirist: The grandmother's recipe returns with the elbow-learning payoff, and the two-guests test can be contradicted. But P1046 and P1047 say the same thing twice. Fold one.

clinician: The Maya kettle close is about mantras, not carrier count; it could sit in another chapter. Earlier landing (P1106, one guest at your elbow) is the kinder end.
habit: The two-guests aim test is a usable rep with a caveat. But Maya's June quarrel is about the kettle line, not carriers, so the ending isn't paid for here.
contemplative: Recipe and Tomas teach carriers well. Maya at the kettle is a different chapter's person, and 1102 repeats 1101. Let it end at the guest beside you.
stress: Carrier count with an honest 'not a measurement' hedge, and a two-guest test. But Maya's kettle story is an orphan that ends on a different subject. Remove or tie to carriers.
gamedesigner: Carrier count and the two-guest test are good. But recipe repeats across P1101-1103, and Maya's ending belongs to the book, not this chapter's argument. Cut or reroute.
structural: Carrier aim is clear, but P1101 and P1102 both retell the recipe. The ending jumps to Maya's quarrel, which isn't about a Turning outliving anyone. Close on Tomas or the elbow.
satirist: Recipe and carrier count are the chapter's honest fact. Then Maya's kettle June arrives from the book's opening and nothing about carriers. End on the elbow, not the callback.
mythmaker: The recipe and Tomas carry the carrier idea. The comfort paragraph repeats the outliving point, and Maya's kettle ending is about something else, a borrowed payoff.

modeler: Carrier count is a real stock, and Tomas and Maya's two carriers pay off. But there is no decay rate or delay; the two-guest test is coarse, though hedged. Name the attrition.
skeptic: Carrier count is a stated, hedged claim ('a reading, not a measurement') with a two-guest test. Maya's return lands modestly. One anecdote still carries much of the weight.
clinician: Tomas and Maya give people; the skip-if-heavy clause is kind. The recipe image repeats across three paragraphs, and the comfort paragraph restates the point before the close.
habit: One question, carrier count, with Tomas as the failure case. The two-guest test is small and hedged. Maya's landing is modest and paid for.
contemplative: Quiet and complete: recipe, Tomas, then Maya and her sister carrying the rule together. Two-guest test is small and honest about its limits. Paragraphs 1101 and 1102 slightly overlap.
stress: P1101 and P1102 both make the recipe-outlives-her point at near-equal strength. Tomas shows a failure case; the two-guest test admits it is rough. Merge the pair.
gamedesigner: Carrier count is a clear, testable mechanic; Tomas shows failure, Maya lands with two carriers. But P1101 and P1102 reuse the recipe, and P1106 repeats the comfort. Merge them.
structural: Carrier count is a clear aim; Tomas shows failure, two-guest test is checkable and hedged. Maya landing earns weight. Rests on recipe analogy, honestly flagged.
satirist: The recipe is a real, bar-table image, and the two-guests test admits its limits. But 1102, 1103 and 1106 re-say outliving; Maya is planted elsewhere, so the landing is borrowed.
mythmaker: Grandmother, Tomas and Maya's sister each carry the idea with something at stake. Ending is quiet and earned: the line gets a second voice. Return to the grandmother's elbow.

C090.label: A. The Mantras, Prayers, and Meditations — Full Text
C090.desc: chapter "A. The Mantras, Prayers, and Meditations — Full Text" (APPENDIX; paragraphs [P1108] to [P1122])

modeler: Eleven lines, grouped choose, steady, check. Closing week-check says what failure looks like. Slightly repetitive early lines, but the ordering builds and the group mantra lands.
skeptic: The one-week check is honest and can fail. The 'stumble or stride' and seed lines overlap, and the closing group line promises more than a recitation can show.
clinician: The week-long check, with a stated way to fail, is useful. The lines overlap (P1054, P1058) and read as a list, not a build. Order them or thin.
habit: The one-week check and the kettle cue turn recitation into a rep. But several lines (stumble or stride, seed) overlap. Pick which line does which job.
contemplative: Short lines, breathable, with a plain check and a return to the kettle. But 'rewoven' and 'stumble or stride' repeat across lines. Pare to one voice per job.
stress: Week-long recited-versus-repeated check is falsifiable. But the lines restate one idea in different words, and the cosmic 'From difference, a shape' close is a bigger payoff than the body earns.
gamedesigner: Week-long check with a did-you-do-it signal is a real fix. But eleven lines are a list, not a build; order is shufflable and the ending is a bare repeat.
structural: Staged five, three, three plus a closing week-check that returns to the kettle. Several mantras restate the stumble-or-stride, step-and-repeat point; differentiate or trim.
satirist: Kettle, doorway and red light are honest, and the new week-check can fail. But P1054 to P1056 are near-twins in liturgical cadence. This is foma and could say so.
mythmaker: The kettle opens it and returns at the close, with a clear order of mantras. Between them there is no face, and some lines repeat each other.

modeler: Lines are a shufflable set, and the intro's 5+4+3 count does not match the thirteen items. The one-week check can fail. Fix the count.
skeptic: Maya's pass-or-fail check and the 'proves nothing more' hedge are honest. The images are flagged as pictures, not evidence. Some lines assert, but the frame is calibrated.
clinician: Lines are short, speak of what you do not what you are, and include a hard-day line. The check can fail and a missed week isn't blamed on the reader.
habit: One line, one pause, one week, and a pass condition of 'even once' that can fail. Maya at the kettle ties it together. Good small rep.
contemplative: One line, one pause, one week; Maya's Monday and Wednesday make the pass real. P1108 is a lot to hold in one breath; shorten.
stress: Text is plain about being handles, not evidence. Maya's missed Monday gives a pass/fail check that can fail. Missed-week reassurance appears twice; one is enough.
gamedesigner: Weekly check with a fail condition is a real feedback loop. But the middle is a long read-only liturgy list, the Maya beat is stranded, and lines blur together.
structural: One line at one pause for a week; Maya's Monday and Wednesday set the pass bar and the check can fail. Grouped lines build to the room.
satirist: Intro admits these are handles, not evidence: Bokonon would nod. The final check can fail, and Maya's bad mornings pay off. But feet-breath-room appears twice doing one job.
mythmaker: Maya's kettle line, the pass/fail check and the 5/4/3 arc give it direction. Several mantras overlap and nobody stands in most of them.

clinician: The die, coastline and phone callback is earned, but 'loop' and 'Third Thing' land together in a for/after map. Define one first.

clinician: Second paragraph cashes in the first's promises cleanly, but it is preview then preview. Nothing new emerges; the pair is a roadmap. Fine for orientation.
habit: Two intro blurbs stacking promises. Q-stack, then 'Third Thing' and 'loop' coined at once. Give one question, one step: 'tonight, note your phone cue.'
contemplative: Two plain signposts; Maya, die and coastline carry across, and Third Thing is named once after loop. But nothing new emerges from the pair. Honest, simply a handrail.
stress: Two previews stacked; Maya, die and coastline are handed across, but nothing is tested yet. Third Thing arrives as a label. Name one condition where the loop claim fails.

structural: Roadmap carries 'loop' and Maya across cleanly, but nothing emerges beyond preview. Name a lever, who rewrites the marriage or habit's rules, to earn a Third Thing.

P0039>P0040.desc: the seam from paragraph [P0039] to paragraph [P0040] (chapter "2. The Third Thing")

modeler: Triangle to wetness to marriage is a jump. Chaos game is a mechanism; marriage is just an analogy riding it.

clinician: Sierpinski jumps to wetness and marriage as 'genuine independent things' in one move. Two new analogies; the jump is not backed.
habit: Dice triangle jumps to wetness and marriages as 'real' independent things. Overreach, two domains. Earn the leap or hedge.
contemplative: From dots on paper to wetness and marriage as 'real' things. The leap is asserted, not shown, and 'hardest idea' is posturing.
